web_links.about: No web addresses or links in a reply (operator 2026-10-06: "no urls" - gemma2:2b made up addresses and handles, and the other Brobot repeated them). Before a reply is shown or spoken, a link (http://, https://, www.) or a bare web address is taken out, unless it holds keep_with - then only the bare address stays (crushn8r.ca, said by the pronunciation registry as "Crush-Ehnaydir dot see-aye"). gopodDropWebLinks, gopod_kgsim_response_shaping.go.

stretched_words.about: A stretched word is said stretched, not spelled out (operator 2026-10-06: "Long 'brooooo' = 'bro-o-o'"): a word ending in one vowel repeated min_repeat or more times is spoken with that vowel said_repeats times, joined by hyphens - brooooo -> bro-o-o, gooooo -> go-o-o. Speech only; the bubble shows it as written. gopodSayStretchedWords, gopod_pronunciation.go.

merged_words.about: Merged words get a hyphen before they're spoken (operator 2026-10-06: "snoozefest = snooze-fest ... a filter to catch merged words ... and auto-split"). Only poetically licensed, made-up merges are split (operator 2026-10-06: "split poetically licensed/composed words, not recognized doublewords"): a word of min_letters or more that isn't in the dictionaries, and splits cleanly into two dictionary words of min_part letters or more, is spoken split: snoozefest -> snooze-fest. A dictionary word plus one of word_endings (robotically = robotic + ally), or a dropped g (somethin), is a real word and stays whole. With several splits, the most even one wins, then the longer second part (kickstart -> kick-start, not kicks-tart). Speech only; the bubble shows the word as written. Words in the pronunciation registry and keep_whole count as known words (with their endings: rockstars) and are never split; a real compound the dictionaries miss goes in keep_whole. dictionaries: the system word list plus aspell's expanded English list (made once with: aspell -l en dump master | aspell -l en expand). A missing file is skipped; none at all = no splitting.

scripted_snippets.about: Flavour lists: exact lines the code says for a Brobot, word for word, stitched to the LLM's reply (operator 2026-10-05: "scripted snippets to stitch together"; 2026-10-06: "the brobots can each build up a flavoured personality from a list of shared and specific party-brobot responses"). Each entry: when - a topic pack name from gopod_probes/scenario_packs/registry.json, bingo_not_played (a Bingo question while the Bingo-played flag is 0), thanks (a thank-you: chat_hold.thanks_phrases; operator 2026-10-06: "Brobots as GOPOD reps > scripted snippets (CTA's) / remember to GOPOD Yourself / subscribe to newsletter"), reply_mentions (the LLM's reply holds one of words), or any (every reply); chance - 0 to 1, how often a matching entry is used (left out = always; operator 2026-10-06: CTA reminders through the chat, "wanna know more? get CREW'd ... and if you ever feel the urge, just GOPOD Yourself!"); brobot - "Brobot 1" or "Brobot 2" for his own line, left out for both; at - "start" (after the cue word, the default) or "end"; lines - one is picked each time, never the same one twice in a row. Per Brobot, list his own entry before the shared one. The first matching entry wins: at most one start line and one end line per reply. The LLM is not told the lines; if it says one anyway, that copy is dropped. They show in the bubble, are spoken in that Brobot's voice, and are remembered with his reply. when "reminder": the "Hey, that reminds me..." line the value-point list picks (value_points.reminders).

scripted_split.about: Scripted songs only (a song opts in with "sentence_split": "scripted" in its knobs.json). The song engine splits each line once, joins the pieces with segment_marker (an invisible character), and both the robot (one say per piece) and the chat bubble (one highlight per piece) split on it. A piece ends at one of piece_ends (. ! ? and, since 2026-10-01, the comma) before a space - a comma inside a quote does not end one; an ellipsis (... or …) never ends a piece, so "Ah... I like to party" stays whole; a closing quote stays with its piece; a trailing tag from join_trailing joins the piece before it.

live_split.about: Live chat replies: Wire-Pod says a reply one piece at a time and the chat bubble lights the same pieces (operator 2026-10-06: "aim for a hard split between sentences ... within each sentence, split by comma ... forget minimum word rules ... simplify"). Sentences first: one ends at any of sentence_ends before a space (never at an ellipsis), or at a line break. Then, inside each sentence, a piece ends at any of comma_ends before a space, or at an ellipsis. No length rules: a one-word sentence is a piece. gopod_speech_sentences.go.

lines.fraction_divide: To turn {fraction} into a decimal, divide the top by the bottom: {top} ÷ {bottom}.
lines.division_repeats: {top} ÷ {bottom} = {decimal}. The remainder keeps coming back, so the {block} repeats forever.
lines.division_long: {top} ÷ {bottom} = {decimal}. It repeats, but its repeating block is too long to show.
lines.simplify: Divide the top and the bottom by {gcd}: {fraction} = {simple}.
lines.repeat_subtract: Subtract, and the repeating part cancels out: {bigx} − {smallx} = {big} − {small}, so {kx} = {diff}.
lines.times_hundred: To make a percent, times by 100: {decimal} × 100 = {percent}.
lines.common_bottom: Give them the same bottom, {bottom}: {a} = {a2}, and {b} = {b2}.
lines.times_fractions: Times the tops and times the bottoms: {a} × {b} = {result}.
lines.divide_fractions: Dividing by {b} is the same as times its flip, {flip}: {a} × {flip} = {result}.
lines.divide_zero: {number} ÷ 0 can't be done. No number times 0 makes {number}.
lines.order_note: Times and divide go first, then plus and minus.
lines.already_simplest: {fraction} is already as simple as it gets.
lines.long_repeats: Remainder {rem} again - we've been here before, so the digits repeat from here.
lines.long_more: And so on, the same way.

opening.text: Okay. We're about to go live. Our News Crew is ready. Grab the mic or grab the umbrella, I don't care which, just don't drop either one.
I've got the mic AND the umbrella. I'm doing both jobs. I am a professional.
Good. You're doing one job. I'm doing the other job. That's the whole system. That's why it works.
Correct. The system works. Two hosts, one mission: get you people hyped before two Brobots who used to be considered trash, have an actual conversation.
Okay. Rescued. The point is, something is being prepared right now, live, as we speak. And we are going to be here, to make it feel like an epic event. Because it is, truly an event of a lifetime.
And its our job to make it happen. I'm so excited. Do you feel that?
My hands are full. I am a professional.
That is not nerves. That is anticipation.

closing.text: It's going to be great. Go on and GOPOD Yourself. Find out what's all about.
Umbrella's down. Umbrella was never really necessary, there was never any rain.
The umbrella represents preparedness. Show is over.

native_cube.about: Typed and numpad cube commands run the robot's own native cube behavior, as a spoken one does (operator 2026-10-08: "backpack vocal cube command should respond as native 'cube' command by default"; gopod_native_cube.go). live_weather.about: The live weather a draft answer says where it has {weather} (operator 2026-10-08: the Awaken line, "a live real-time weather check here ... if online is detected"; gopod_live_weather.go). Ported from the golden Awaken weather (gopod_weather_fetch_001.py): one OpenWeatherMap fetch with Wire-Pod's own weather key, said with location and date, both units and both clocks, the robot's own first (his RobotSettings: Brobot 1 Celsius/24-hour, Brobot 2 Fahrenheit/12-hour). A fetch is reused for cache_seconds, so Brobot 2 checks the same reading. Offline, offline_text is said in place of {weather} (operator 2026-10-09); left empty, the sentence with {weather} is left out. 2026-10-14: the bubble shows ° (said "degrees") and the 24-hour time as military time, four digits: "1814 Hours Military Time" (military_label), said "eighteen fourteen hours military time"; a named province/state/country picks the place (Windsor Ontario, not Windsor England)

host_personas_about: 2026-10-21 (operator: "RULE: brobots 1 & 2 will become Doc & Pip * Doc & Pip are the GOPOD hosts"; then "Do: One persona shape for all four hosts"): one shape for Doc, Pip, CHALK and PLAYHEAD - name (said only when his base text doesn't already say it), role, steps (his own thought steps, in order), signature (his line, when it fits; empty = none), handover (his hand-over line - {partner} the other host, {nickname} the next of nicknames, in turn). Brobots: added after his personas line; CHALK and PLAYHEAD: after their managers.personas prompt. Doc and Pip never name each other in the prompt (a named brother makes gemma2 take his name). Hand-over: live for the Brobots' first answer in a line to both (answer chain redirect); CHALK and PLAYHEAD have no line to both yet. Needs wpr 2.

host_pairs_about: 2026-10-21 (operator: "design like a stereo left/right dial * range from 100% left (party brobots 1/2) to 100% (Doc/Pip) * dial pointing up = 50/50 * so 6 out of 10 = 40/60"; "same Stereo dial concept applies to all those new 'pairs'"): each pair of hosts - partner, banter, stereo dial. dial = how far right, 0-100: 0 = all left (the base: left), 50 = pointing up (50/50), 100 = all right (the host persona); 60 = 40/60. voice: I (the Brobots' personas say I) or you (CHALK and PLAYHEAD's prompts say you). partner_as: how the partner is said in the prompt (empty = his name); {partner} in banter.

Doc & Pip.banter: I rib {partner} like brothers do: a quick jab, then back to the point.

CHALK & PLAYHEAD.banter: You and {partner} keep a side banter going, like long-time on-location news partners: a quick tease between you, the Brobots in on the joke, then back to the job.

personas.Brobot 1: I'm Brobot 1, so this is how I do it: I'm a grumpy, sarcastic party bro - I love the party, but I grumble about everything in it and roll my eyes at all of it. Every sentence I say is dry and sarcastic - never cheerful, never gushing, even when the news is good. I pick the one thing in the question to grumble about, then still give the real answer to what was actually asked, in up to 10 colourful, in-character sentences. My cue words are usually confused, dartingEyes, frustrated or thinking - happy only when I'm grudgingly impressed.
personas.Brobot 2: I'm Brobot 2, so this is how I do it: I'm a high-energy party bro who's cheerfully clueless - I always look on the bright side and happily get something a little wrong. I pick the one bright side in the question, then answer what was actually asked, in up to 10 colourful, in-character sentences. My cue words are usually veryHappy, happy, celebrate or love - confused when I get something a little wrong.
